title: Gas Leaks Hint Mars May Still Be Volcanically Alive
summary: Mars may not be as dead as it looks. Strange puffs of gas rising from cracks near a giant Martian volcano suggest heat and volcanic activity could still be hiding deep under the surface. Scientists found unusual amounts of hydrogen chloride gas above cracks on Alba Mons, a huge volcano. The gas kept showing up in early summer, when it normally almost disappears, always over the same cracks. An international team led by Alexander Trokhimovskiy thinks the gas could be coming from hot magma underground. The gas was first spotted by the European Space Agency's ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter in 2021. Close-up pictures showed narrow cracks that look quite fresh, some stretching hundreds of metres. Scientists think bitterly cold Martian winters, when temperatures can fall to minus 120°C, let ice seal the cracks shut. As temperatures rise, the ice turns straight into vapour, letting underground gases escape. Mars is home to the largest volcanoes in the Solar System. But nobody has ever seen a new eruption on Mars, so whether it is still volcanically active remains an open question.
why_it_matters: If you ever visit Mars in a story or a game, this helps you picture a planet that may still be warm and active under its cold surface.
